LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASS: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we use possessive forms correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify possessive forms in print or digital texts
2. use possessive forms correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASS: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASS: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify possessive forms in print or digital texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify possessive forms in print or digital texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify possessive forms in print or digital texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify possessive forms in print or digital texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use possessive forms correctly in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use possessive forms correctly in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use possessive forms correctly in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use possessive forms correctly in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify possessive forms in print or digital texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns to a partner. (skill: use possessive forms correctly in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify possessive forms in print or digital texts.
3. Practise this skill: use possessive forms correctly in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we use possessive forms correctly?
2. Which words show something belongs to a person?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify possessive forms in print or digital texts.
5. Be able to: use possessive forms correctly in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
